newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE STUDENTS BOYCOTT CLASS FOR HIGHER GRANTS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE STUDENTS BOYCOTT CLASS FOR HIGHER GRANTS.

text.p: Students from Zimbabwe's University of Science and Technology started aclass boycott on Monday demanding a 55 percent rise in government grants.
The students, in the southwestern city of Bulawayo, said the $107 monthly payout was inadequate.
"We would need at least Z$2,500 (U.S.245) to buy all the necessities and remain with some money for incidentals," one student said.
The Ministry of Higher Education said in a statement it did not budget for student grant increases in its annual national budget presented in July.
In August, Zimbabwean civil servants went on strike demanding salary hikes of between 30 and 60 percent, dismissing as an insult earlier offers of up to nine percent.

President Robert Mugabe's cash-strapped government later agreed to award them 20 percent on top of what had already been offered. But last Friday the state news agency, ZIANA, reported Mugabe and his cabinet had more than doubled their salaries and allowances backdated to July.
